subtitle: The Circular Product Builder
intro: I'm the one who builds profitable products that are climate-positive.
body: The best products come from pains you've actually lived. Mine: being a second-hand-first buyer, a zero-waste nerd who keeps running into missing solutions for everyday life. That's why I'm drawn to building products that turn resources nobody wants anymore into something worth paying for.

I've spent my whole professional life building products — first coding and delivering as a software developer, now discovering, prototyping and testing as a Product Manager, proving, every time, that circular doesn't mean less profitable.
closingQuote: I work at the intersection of product thinking, hands-on building, and climate — and I make decisions that hold all three at once.

items.text: I ask customers the right questions — and turn the answers into insight, not just notes.
I decide what's in and out of an MVP.
I map the opportunity tree and justify why one solution wins over the rest.
I can tell when an experiment worked — and when it didn't.
I align engineering, design and leadership behind a single priority — even when they walked in with three different ones.
I build the business case alongside the user case, so "nice to have" never wins by default.
I troubleshoot bugs once they ship.
I size the effort behind a spec before anyone commits to a deadline.
I know my way around a Docker deployment on AWS — enough to work with engineering, not just manage around them.
I vibe-code prototypes to test ideas fast.
I read how a decision moves the needle on climate — for better or worse.
I weigh that against corporate values — not just check the box on them.
